rmt-2006-power-01.prompt: **Hackenbush** (idea from *Winning Ways*) is a game for two players, Blue and Red, played with a picture consisting of straight and wavy edges connected to each other and to the ground. Blue moves by deleting any straight edge, together with any edges that are then no longer connected to the ground. Red moves by similarly deleting a wavy edge. A player with no edge left to delete loses. Both players always make the best possible moves. Who wins in each of the following games (a)-(d)? (In (a) the straight edges form a vertical segment with a triangle and a diagonal leg; in (d) the wavy part is a vertical wavy path with a wavy arm.)
rmt-2006-power-01.answer: (a) Blue wins; (b) Red wins; (c) Red wins; (d) neither player has an advantage: the second player to move wins (it is a zero game).
rmt-2006-power-01.reviewNote: The official key says Blue for (d), but (d) has 3 straight and 3 wavy edges, so it is a zero game (value 0) and the second player wins; the key's own value 0 for (d) in Problem 3 agrees. The key's answer for (d) seems left over from the pre-correction version of the test.

rmt-2006-power-02.prompt: **Hackenbush** (idea from *Winning Ways*) is a game for two players, Blue and Red, played with a picture consisting of straight and wavy edges connected to each other and to the ground. Blue moves by deleting any straight edge, together with any edges that are then no longer connected to the ground. Red moves by similarly deleting a wavy edge. A player with no edge left to delete loses. Both players always make the best possible moves. Find a winning strategy for one of the players in the following game (the picture shows two trees on the ground: the left one has a wavy tent at the bottom, a straight stem, and a hub with four straight and two wavy edges; the right one is its color-swapped copy). For what other games will your strategy ensure a win for one of the players?
rmt-2006-power-02.answer: The second player wins by mirroring each move in the color-swapped copy. The strategy works for every game of the form $G+\overline G$, where $\overline G$ is $G$ with all colors swapped (also if the two halves are connected).

rmt-2006-power-03.prompt: **Hackenbush** (idea from *Winning Ways*) is a game for two players, Blue and Red, played with a picture consisting of straight and wavy edges connected to each other and to the ground. Blue moves by deleting any straight edge, together with any edges that are then no longer connected to the ground. Red moves by similarly deleting a wavy edge. A player with no edge left to delete loses. Both players always make the best possible moves. **Value.** The *value* of a game is a number associated with it so that: (i) a single straight edge on the ground has value $1$ and a single wavy edge has value $-1$; (ii) a game in which the first player to move always loses (a *zero game*) has value $0$; (iii) for games $G,H$ with values $g,h$ placed side by side, the value of the whole game $G+H$ is $g+h$. (You may assume these properties are consistent; a game has value $v$ if it is worth $v$ moves.) Find the value of each of the games (a)-(d) shown in Problem 1 (see the figure) and of the game of Problem 2 (two color-swapped trees).
rmt-2006-power-03.answer: (a) $3$, (b) $-3$, (c) $-1$, (d) $0$; the game of Problem 2 has value $0$.
